title: How do we place a square in the middle of a rectangle?
description: A rectangle eight centimetres by four centimetres is drawn, and a square is constructed inside it with the same centre. The side of the square and the gap on each side are worked out from the lengths.
teaching_notes: One idea: a square that touches the top and bottom has the breadth as its side, and the leftover length is shared equally on both sides. Watch for students who put the square in one corner instead of sharing the leftover length.

source: Construct 1: A Square within a Rectangle (section 8.4)
video_script.why: A learner constructs a square inside a rectangle so that both share the same centre.
video_script.substitution: the same way as the example in your book: squares built on a rectangle's length from its breadth
video_script.anchor: a rectangle eight centimetres by four centimetres with a square drawn in its middle
video_script.payoff_line: The square sits two centimetres in from each short side.

final_answer.value: The square has side 4 cm. Its left and right sides are 2 cm away from the left and right sides of the rectangle
final_answer.spoken: two centimetres in from each short side

maths_rules: the square touches the top and bottom, so its side = the breadth of the rectangle = 4 cm
8 cm − 4 cm = 4 cm is left over along the length
4 cm shared equally on both sides: 4 cm ÷ 2 = 2 cm on each side
video_script.design: The rectangle is drawn, the square side is read from the breadth, the leftover length is shared equally, and the sum is checked.
